PROMISE: National Traders’ Welfare Board/ National Retail Trade Policy
STATUS AND COMMENTS: India established the National Traders’ Welfare Board (NTWB) in 2023. The NTWB's objectives include identifying policy measures for the welfare of traders and their employees, suggesting simplifications in the Acts and Rules applicable to traders, and advising on social security benefits for traders. The Board consists of various members representing different facets of trade and government. However, the National Retail Trade Policy in India has not yet been fully implemented. The BJP-led government has made strides in implementing a single-window system that indirectly benefits MSMEs.

The BJP's promise on tax reforms included corporate tax cuts, reducing the effective income tax for corporations from 34.94% to 25.17%. The minimum alternate tax was also reduced from 18.5% to 15%. Despite these cuts costing the exchequer about Rs 1.84 lakh crore over two years, the impact on economic growth and compliance has been debated.

The Companies (Amendment) Act, 2020, focused on decriminalizing various offenses under the Companies Act, 2013, shifting certain offenses from criminal to civil jurisdiction. It introduced in-house adjudication mechanisms and proposed the removal of imprisonment penalties for specific offenses, opting for monetary penalties. There's also a reduction in penalties related to financial statements and corporate social responsibility. These amendments aim to reduce the legal burden on corporations.
